comparison: Perfect agreement on study design and methodology (C18-C20, C25-C27, C94). Both OpenEval and peer reviewers affirm this is the first nationwide survey in Bolivia with a large representative sample. Both evaluate the study design as well-documented and supported.

Perfect agreement on seroprevalence findings (C35-C41, C98). Both OpenEval and peer reviewers find the serological data solid and well-supported, with consistent interpretation of antibody prevalence patterns indicating natural infection.

Divergent evaluations on hybrid immunity estimates (C42-C43). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to lack of explicit methodology for calculating these values, while peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED and recognize the contribution to understanding hybrid immunity without raising methodological concerns.

Perfect agreement on neutralization data (C44-C65). Both OpenEval and peer reviewers affirm the comprehensive neutralization assays with GMTs and prevalence data. Both find the variant-specific patterns logical and well-supported by the data.

Strong agreement on Gamma variant spatiotemporal analysis (C66-C70, C75-C77). Both evaluations support the geographic circulation patterns and integration with vaccination data. Peer review includes C99 which addresses broader geographic insights.

Perfect agreement on Delta and Omicron BA.1 detection (C71-C74, C78-C79). Both OpenEval and peer reviewers accept the temporal patterns and emergence of these variants as supported by neutralization data and alignment with regional genomic surveillance.

Agreement on UNCERTAIN evaluation for speculative interpretations (C80-C82, C84-C86). Both OpenEval and peer reviewers express concern about inferring timing estimates and mechanisms from neutralization data due to heterogeneous effects of infections and vaccination. OpenEval specifically questions antigenic sin and antibody boosting claims as speculative.

Strong agreement on methodological validation (C87-C89, C102). Both evaluations affirm the convergent validation across multiple analytical approaches and alignment with independent genomic data. Peer review additionally includes C121 on genomic alignment.

Strong agreement on methodological conclusions and limitations (C90-C93, C97, C104). Both evaluations support the conclusions about optimal timing for seroepidemiological studies and acknowledge limitations regarding accuracy over time. Peer review additionally includes C137 on increasing complexity.

Agreement on antigenic grouping approach (C109-C121). Both evaluations support the systematic antigenic grouping methodology and its validation through detection of variant emergence. OpenEval emphasizes all claims C109-C121, while peer review groups these with individual variant quantification claims C122-C129.

Agreement on individual variant quantification (C122-C129). Both evaluations support the detailed analytical approaches for detecting individual variants. OpenEval focuses on these specific claims while peer review groups them with the broader antigenic grouping methodology.

Perfect agreement on vaccination coverage data (C28-C34). Both evaluations accept these descriptive statistics as appropriate contextual information for interpreting serological findings, with no concerns raised.

Agreement on study limitations (C130-C131, C135-C136). Both evaluations view the acknowledgment of limitations as appropriate and scientifically rigorous. OpenEval includes additional claims C132-C134 about representativeness validation.

Perfect agreement on epidemiological background (C1-C17). Both evaluations accept the contextual information establishing study rationale and knowledge gaps without question. These claims provide standard background framing.
Perfect agreement on vaccination policy context (C21-C24). Both evaluations accept this descriptive information about Bolivia's vaccination program as necessary context for interpreting findings.
Agreement on public health implications (C95-C96). Both evaluations support the broad conclusions about seroprevalence studies' value. Peer review additionally includes C103 on broader implications.

Agreement on methodological details (C105-C108). Both evaluations accept the quality control measures and assay interpretation criteria as appropriate. Peer review additionally includes C109 on antigenic grouping literature basis.

Partial overlap on contextual claims. OpenEval R13 addresses study limitations including representativeness validation (C132-C134), while peer R17 groups these representativeness claims with other contextual information (C83) as accepted without question.
